verdict.rationale: pnpm documents offline installs from its content-addressable store (`pnpm i --offline`, and a setting that fails the install if a package isn't found locally), and it has a CI docs page covering frozen-lockfile behavior. Community users report fast CI installs with a smaller cache (15s vs 35s). However, the evidence never shows a documented cache-restore recipe for CI, such as which store path to cache or a CI provider cache configuration. missing for 10: documented CI cache-restore setup (store path / cache key guidance), first-party CI speed benchmarks or corroboration tied to a cache recipe

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can make CI installs fast with a documented cache-restore setup and offline-capable installs

citations.quote: `pnpm i --offline` Install offline from the store only
If true, pnpm will use only packages already available in the store. If a package won't be found locally, the installation will fail.
When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.
It works very fast in CI. Its cache is smaller and it builds node_modules much faster.
